title: Multi-level precise regulation of gene transcription in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae based on light-sensitive CRISPR/Cas systems.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Read the full open-access text (75,986 characters) including the data availability statement and methods. Checked Europe PMC and NCBI for deposited data: no accessions anywhere in the text, no text-mined accessions, no GEO/SRA/BioProject links, no Zenodo/Dryad hit on the DOI, and the flag for database cross-references is 'N'. Tried the Europe PMC supplementary-files endpoint three times (one HTTP 500, two timeouts) and could not retrieve it.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: That the supplement contains only Supplementary Table S1 (DNA fragments: promoter variants, EL222, VP16, VP64, terminators) and Supplementary Table S2 (Sanger-verified sequences of the constructed fragments), plus six supplementary figures; that all measurements are fluorescence readings from about 17 engineered yeast strains, each repeated three times, reported as mean +/- standard deviation in bar charts made in GraphPad Prism.

a1_downloadable.note: No data deposit exists: data availability says only 'available in the article and in its online supplementary material'. The supplement itself was not retrievable (Europe PMC supplementary-files endpoint returned HTTP 500 once and timed out twice), and per the paper it holds DNA sequences, not a measurement table. The actual numbers live inside figure bar charts.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: The prediction target (mCherry or mEYFP fluorescence intensity under blue light versus dark) is nowhere a column. It exists only as plotted bars in Figures 1-6 and Supplementary Figures S1-S6, so it would have to be constructed by digitising graphs - the clearest possible A2 failure.

a3_inputs_present.note: Paper text only (file not opened): Supplementary Tables S1 and S2 are said to list the DNA sequences of all promoter variants and constructed fragments, so the input sequences would be present if the supplement were retrievable.

a4_units_stated.note: Fluorescence is reported as relative/fold-change values and 'relative fluorescence units' from a plate reader, with no stated absolute unit and no calibration; values are only comparable within a figure panel.

a5_enough_rows.note: The study builds roughly 17 yeast strains (Strains 1-17 are named in the results) measured in a handful of light/dark conditions, three biological replicates each - on the order of tens to a few hundred data points, far under the ~400-row minimum even for classification.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Not assessed in depth after the killer failures; the entire dataset is a few dozen numbers, so size was never the issue.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: Not assessable: there is no downloadable data file whose counts could be compared against the paper.

a8_label_provenance.note: The label is a direct physical measurement (fluorescence of mCherry/mEYFP in live yeast), not another model's output, so A8 itself is fine - the project dies on A1/A2/A5 instead.

honest_claim_h3: No honest modelling claim is available: with roughly 17 engineered strains whose readouts exist only as bar charts, any model would be fitting a few dozen hand-digitised numbers.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use engineered DNA part combinations to predict how strongly blue light switches a yeast gene on or off
plain_idea.train_on: The project considered would give the model the DNA parts of each engineered yeast strain (which activation domain, how many light-responsive promoter copies, which RNA-binding motif upstream of the dCas9 gene) for roughly 17 strains - a number read from the results text, not from a file.
plain_idea.predict: The output would be the light-induced change in red or yellow fluorescent protein brightness, measured in a plate reader on yeast cultures grown under repeating 70-second-light/30-second-dark cycles, three replicates per strain.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Synthetic biology groups building light-controlled gene circuits would like to pick part combinations without building each one, but this paper supplies far too few examples to learn that mapping.

ml_idea: Considered and rejected: predict light-induced fold-change in fluorescent-protein output from the DNA part composition of light-controlled CRISPR interference circuits in yeast. The dataset is roughly 17 strains with readings only in figures, so there is nothing to train on.

effort.compute_note: Estimated, nothing timed: the entire dataset is a few dozen fluorescence values, so compute was never a constraint - the constraint is that the values are not in machine-readable form.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Count the distinct measured strains in the paper (about 17) before anything else; that single count kills the project in five minutes.

verdict_reason: A wet-lab optogenetics/CRISPR engineering paper with no deposited data: about 17 engineered yeast strains, measurements only as bar charts in figures, supplement limited to DNA sequences. Fails A1 (no data file), A2 (label must be digitised from graphs), A4 (relative fluorescence units only) and A5 (tens of data points, not thousands).
